facts.subject: language
facts.text: Linguists debate whether the language you speak shapes how you think. This idea is called linguistic relativity.

facts.subject: language
facts.text: In most languages, the most common word is used about twice as often as the second most common one. This is called Zipf's law.

facts.subject: language
facts.text: English, Hindi, Spanish and Russian all come from one ancient ancestor language, Proto-Indo-European.

facts.subject: language
facts.text: Code-switching is when a speaker moves between two languages or ways of speaking in the same conversation.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: In 1931, Kurt Gödel proved that in any consistent system of arithmetic there are true statements that cannot be proved.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: Fermat's Last Theorem, posed in the 1600s, was finally proved by Andrew Wiles in the 1990s.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: Euler's identity connects five of the most important numbers in maths: 0, 1, e, i and pi.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: Euclid proved more than 2,000 years ago that there are infinitely many prime numbers.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for CRISPR, a tool for editing genes.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: The Higgs boson was discovered at CERN in 2012.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: The second law of thermodynamics says that entropy, a measure of disorder, tends to increase in an isolated system.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: Mitochondria make most of the chemical energy (ATP) that cells use.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: In the 2015 Paris Agreement, countries agreed to try to keep global warming well below 2 degrees Celsius.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: The Human Development Index compares countries using life expectancy, education and income.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations in 1948.

source.title: Wikipedia: Universal Declaration of Human Rights

facts.subject: world
facts.text: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the 18th century.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: The World Health Organization defines health as more than the absence of disease: it includes physical, mental and social well-being.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: Your gut is home to trillions of microbes, called the gut microbiota.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: Your body clock, the circadian rhythm, runs on a cycle of about 24 hours.

facts.subject: health
facts.text: Antibiotic resistance happens when bacteria change so that medicines no longer kill them.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: Public-key cryptography lets two people who have never met share secret messages safely.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: Algorithmic bias is when a computer system gives unfair results, often because of the data it learned from.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: The EU's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) came into force in 2018 and gives people rights over their personal data.

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: AI chatbots can state false things with confidence. This is often called hallucination, so important facts should be checked.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best choice you give up when you decide.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: The rule of 72 says that dividing 72 by an interest rate in percent gives roughly how many years it takes to double your money.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: In a market, when something is scarce and many people want it, its price tends to rise. This is supply and demand.

facts.subject: money
facts.text: The symbol for the Indian rupee was officially adopted in 2010.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: The Dunning-Kruger effect is the finding that people with little skill at something often overestimate how good they are.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: Survivorship bias is when we only look at the cases that survived. In World War II, Abraham Wald used this idea to decide where to armour aircraft.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: In the Monty Hall problem, switching doors wins two-thirds of the time.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: The trolley problem is a famous thought experiment used to explore ethics.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart began composing music at the age of five.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: Impressionism got its name from a painting by Claude Monet called Impression, Sunrise.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: William Shakespeare wrote about 37 plays.

facts.subject: arts
facts.text: The Eiffel Tower in Paris was finished in 1889.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: Whether every problem whose answer can be checked quickly can also be solved quickly (P versus NP) is a Millennium Prize problem worth a million dollars.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: A quantum computer uses qubits, which can be in a superposition of 0 and 1.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: Many computers count time as the seconds since 1 January 1970.

facts.subject: computing
facts.text: Git, a tool programmers use to track changes in code, was created by Linus Torvalds in 2005.
